overview.description: LegacyHQ uses a three-tier token architecture to create a scalable, maintainable, and themeable design system while minimizing duplicate meanings.

tiers.name: Primitive Tokens
rules: Primitive tokens contain raw values only.
Primitive tokens must not represent intent.
Components must never consume primitive tokens directly.

tiers.name: Semantic Tokens
rules: Semantic tokens should be the primary tokens consumed throughout the system.
Semantic tokens map to primitive tokens.
New semantic tokens should only be created when a new meaning is introduced.

tiers.name: Component Tokens
rules: Component tokens are exceptions, not defaults.
Component tokens should generally alias semantic tokens.
Exception: a component dimension token may alias the primitive scale when it represents geometry unique to that component (see dimensions.componentTokenException).
Component tokens should only exist when a component requires independent control, theming, or behavior.

componentTokenCreationRule.description: Before creating a component token, determine whether the semantic layer already expresses the needed meaning.
steps: Determine whether a semantic token already expresses the same meaning.
Reuse the semantic token whenever possible.
Create a component token only when the semantic layer cannot adequately express the requirement.

ifEquivalentSemanticTokenExists.rule: If an equivalent semantic token exists, do not create a new component token.

avoidExample.allowedOnlyWhen: There is a documented need for independent control.

interactionStateVocabulary.summary: One canonical word per interaction state, used identically in Figma variable names, generated CSS custom properties, component variant axes, and the data-force-state escape hatch. Unified across Figma and code together - there is no longer a past-participle form anywhere.
rules: Use the bare-verb form: hover (not hover), press (not press), focus (not focus).
A token whose name ends in a state uses exactly one of these words, e.g. color.background.neutral.overlay.bold.hover / .bold.press, color.border.focus, color.border.selected.
The Storybook data-force-state escape hatch takes the same vocabulary: data-force-state="hover" | "focus" | "press". It is documentation-only and never part of a public API.
notCovered: CSS pseudo-classes are browser primitives and keep their own spelling: :hover, :focus-visible, :active. Only our own names follow this vocabulary - :active is the platform selector that implements the press state.
ARIA attributes keep their spec spelling: aria-press, aria-selected, aria-disabled, aria-busy.
ProgressIndicator step progress uses an unrelated data-state="active|complete|incomplete" axis - that is step position, not interaction, and is out of scope for this vocabulary.
Grammatical English prose in comments and docs is unaffected ("tinted while hovered" is prose, not an identifier).

antiPatterns: Component tokens that mirror existing semantic tokens.
Component tokens that reference primitive values directly - except dimension tokens for geometry unique to one component (see dimensions.componentTokenException).
Creating tokens for a single isolated use case.
Creating semantic tokens that differ only by component name.

questions: Can an existing semantic token be reused?
Will multiple components share this meaning?
Does the token represent meaning or implementation?
decisionFramework.defaultDecision: If a semantic token already expresses the meaning, reuse it.
decisionFramework.principle: When in doubt, prefer fewer tokens with clearer intent.

dimensions.description: Which family a dimension token belongs to, and how to choose one. Documented for people in Storybook at Foundations / Spacing.

primitiveScale.rule: Raw lengths with no intent. Component CSS never references them.
primitiveScale.figmaNaming: Figma names these primitives number/*. The repo keeps measurement-*; whether to align the names is a separate token-source decision.

families.definition: Spacing describes distance between, inside, or relative to elements when that distance expresses layout relationship.
Negative spacing for elements that deliberately stack, such as the avatars in an Avatar Group.
The dimensions of elements themselves. Use the most specific family that fits; the numeric scale (100 = 8px) covers any other element dimension.
Corner radius and stroke width - separate families even when a value matches a spacing step.
families.strokeRule: Border-width tokens define stroke thickness regardless of rendering technique: border, outline, inset/outset shadow, divider, indicator, or SVG stroke.
families.blurredShadows: A blurred shadow is elevation, not a stroke. An unblurred shadow (offset or spread only) is a stroke and takes its thickness from border-width tokens.

techniques.border: The stroke is there at rest and part of the element's box.
techniques.insetShadow: The stroke appears or thickens with state and content must not move, sits inside padding without resizing the element, or is painted over content.
techniques.outsetShadow: A ring outside an element that must not change its size (spread only).
techniques.outline: Keyboard focus, through the Focus Ring primitive.
techniques.element: A line of its own (divider, indicator), sized with a border-width token.

families.emphasisStroke: A stroke that thickens with state without moving content is an inset shadow of calc(var(--border-width-md) - var(--border-width-sm)) inside the resting border, so the visual stroke is md.
families.radiusNotes: border-radius-md (5px) is used only by Rich Text Area's slash input and by no Figma component; whether to retire it is a separate design decision.

families.definition: Geometry only one component has, such as Switch's thumb travel or Menu's widths.

dimensions.rule: Choose a dimension token by what the value does, not by the number it resolves to: 16px of padding is spacing-lg, and a 16px-tall element is size-200. If the right family doesn't have the value, raise it as a gap rather than borrowing a primitive or another family's token.
notSpacing: type metrics such as line height
dimensions.componentTokenException: Component tokens may alias primitives when they represent geometry unique to one component. Do not create semantic tokens only so component tokens have something to alias. Component CSS itself must never consume primitives.

rawLengths.rule: Not every numeric length needs a token. Separate values that reveal a missing reusable token from acceptable local or layout arithmetic.
acceptable: one-off geometry local to one component

dimensions.enforcement: Not enforced yet. Foundations / Spacing lists, live from component CSS, the places where spacing is missing, misclassified, or borrowed for a non-spacing purpose.

spacing: There is no focus-ring offset token: several components set --focus-ring-offset or outline-offset with spacing tokens, and Focus Ring and Table set a raw 2px.
Rich Text Area's slash-command picker shadow falls back to spacing tokens for its offset and blur, because the --elevation-shadow-overlay token it refers to doesn't exist.
Link sets its icon line-height with --spacing-none.
sizingAndLayout: Table row heights (32, 40, and 64px) are raw lengths repeated across Table, Text Field (editable table cells), and Time Picker (table-cell footer), with no shared token.
Panel and dialog widths are raw lengths in Date Picker and Time Picker (240px), Toast and Toast Group (368px), and Modal Dialog (400-968px), while Menu and Tooltip widths are component tokens.
openFindings.note: The spacing findings also appear on Foundations / Spacing, and shape exceptions would appear on Foundations / Radius, both generated from component CSS. The sizing and layout findings are recorded only here; they are not spacing issues.
shape: None in component CSS (2026-10-08): no raw radius or stroke values, no shape primitives, and every stroke-like shadow takes its thickness from border-width tokens.

Figma: most component strokes bind deleted variables (border/width/default, 🌮 Stroke) and pills use raw radii (10000, 8333, 1198.8) instead of border/radius/full-round; tracked as a separate Figma clean-up.

elevation.description: How visual depth is expressed. Documented for people in Storybook at Foundations / Elevation.
elevation.surfaceColor: Surface color expresses depth within the page: color-elevation-surface-deep, -sunken, -default (the page), and -raised, each with hover and press. Raised surfaces rest on the page and cast no shadow; their border separates them.
elevation.shadow: An elevation shadow indicates that a surface floats above the interface. Use the role token; never rebuild a shadow from the color-elevation-shadow-* colors in component CSS. A floating surface keeps its border; the shadow sits outside it.

roles.source: DTCG shadow composite in Semantic: Elevation (semantic-elevation-light.json and -dark.json), so light.css and dark.css each declare it and its colors resolve per theme.
roles.layers: inset 0 0 0 border-width-sm in color-elevation-shadow-overlay-inner (transparent in both themes); 0 8px 12px 0 in -spread; 0 0 1px 0 in -perimeter.
usedBy: Popup (and Dropdown Menu, Select, Date Picker, Time Picker, Inline Message through it)

elevation.strokeComposition: Shape owns stroke thickness. Elevation may compose a Shape stroke into a shadow recipe, as the overlay inner ring does with border-width-sm. Blurred shadow layers are elevation; unblurred standalone rings and strokes remain Shape.
elevation.notYet: Figma defines raised and overflow effect styles and their colors exist as tokens, but no component uses them, so they have no composite. Add one only when a component needs it.

unused.primitives: shadow-sm/md/lg-x/y/blur/spread (12): no token or component uses them; kept for now.

elevation.layering: Stacking order (z-index) is a separate concern: it is not paired with elevation and isn't tokenized yet.

findings: Popup-based overlays (z-index 1) render behind an open Modal Dialog (z-index 1000); Toast Group and Modal Dialog tie at 1000. Tracked as a separate layering task.

Four Light taupe alpha primitives (alpha-1100-12/16/24/32) are twice as opaque as their names and Figma (0.16/0.32/0.48/0.64), so the Light overlay shadow renders at 32%/64% instead of Figma's 16%/32%, and Light border-default and press fills are affected too. Tracked separately.
Storybook applies the theme to a wrapper div, so portaled overlays (Popup, Modal Dialog) render with Light tokens in Dark mode. Tracked separately.
Figma: color/elevation/shadow/overlay/spread and /perimeter don't exist as variables, and the effect styles aren't bound to variables (they hard-code the same values).

motion.description: How motion is built and applied. Documented for people in Storybook at Foundations / Motion. Motion is code-only: Figma has no motion variables, and its prototypes set their own timings.
motion.primitives: Durations (duration-fast 150ms, duration-slow 300ms, duration-loop 860ms, duration-loop-slow 1500ms) and easings (ease-standard, which never overshoots; ease-spring, which overshoots to about 110% before settling; ease-loop). Component CSS never uses them directly.

recipes.rule: Components use recipes: a duration and an easing in one value, used whole in a transition or an animation, once for each property that changes. Never add a timing function after a recipe: the declaration becomes invalid and the browser drops it. Modal Dialog's entrance never ran because of this.
recipes.fade: fade-* uses the standard non-overshooting motion curve for visual state changes: color, opacity, and indicators that turn or grow (Select's caret, Progress Bar's and Progress Tracker's fills).
recipes.move: move-* uses the spring curve for physical movement of an element: Switch's thumb, Slider's handle, Avatar's selection ring, and Toast Group's stack.
recipes.duration: quick is duration-fast (150ms), for direct feedback; long is duration-slow (300ms), for larger choreography such as the toast stack.
recipes.loops: spin-loop (Spinner) and pulse-loop (Skeleton) repeat an animation. pulse-loop holds a literal linear curve rather than an easing primitive.
recipes.delay: No recipe has a delay and no component adds one. Add a delay only when there's a real need.

motion.hover: High-frequency, direct hover feedback may be instant: Menu and Table rows, Link, Avatar Group, and Inline Edit change on hover with no transition. More prominent state changes use fade-quick.
motion.overlays: Overlays enter using fade-quick; individual components may add local keyframed choreography, such as Modal Dialog's 8px rise. Popup and Modal Dialog leave at once. Toast Group uses move-long for the stack's movement and fade-long for toasts appearing and leaving.
motion.progress: Progress uses fade-quick, never a spring or movement recipe: it's a state change, not physical movement.
motion.componentMotion: Keyframes and choreography stay local to the component, timed with a recipe. There are no component motion tokens.
motion.distance: How far something travels is component geometry, not a motion or spacing token: a component dimension token when it's tied to the component's sizes (Switch's thumb travel), otherwise local (Modal Dialog's 8px rise, Toast Group's stack offsets).
motion.timers: A JavaScript timer that waits for motion should match the recipe's duration: Toast Group's EXIT_MS is 300, duration-slow, and a test keeps them in step.

reducedMotion.rule: Every component that moves responds to prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. The state still changes, without the movement: transitions finish at once (transition-duration: 0ms), loops stop (animation: none), and entrances don't play (animation-duration: 0ms, or the animation is added only inside a no-preference block, as Modal Dialog does).
reducedMotion.selectors: A reduce block must list every selector that adds motion. A media query adds no specificity, so a more specific moving rule elsewhere wins; Toast Group's .item[data-swiping='true'] did until it was listed.
reducedMotion.spinner: Spinner stops rather than turning slowly, and shows a still arc.

motion.naming: Recipes say quick/long while the duration primitives say fast/slow, and the loop durations are duration-loop and duration-loop-slow. Left as is for now.
motion.enforcement: Not mechanically enforced yet: stylelint doesn't gate transition or animation values. The Motion page lists, from component CSS, raw timings, a recipe followed by a timing function, motion that reduced motion doesn't switch off, motion primitives used directly, and missing motion tokens. Modal Dialog, Toast Group, and Progress Bar tests pin their own motion. Candidates for later: those checks as lint or tests, and JavaScript exit timers derived from the CSS duration.

findings: Figma prototypes use their own timings, which differ from code: Switch's thumb is 200ms ease-in-out in Figma and move-quick (150ms spring) in code; Menu's hover is 300ms ease-out in Figma and instant in code. With no motion variables in Figma, there's nothing to reconcile against yet.

enforcement.description: This governance doc is a convention, not a guarantee. Raw-value regressions in component CSS are caught mechanically by stylelint, not by review alone.

gated: padding, margin, and gap (and their longhands)

notGated.reason: These frequently require geometric arithmetic (calc(), negative offsets) that doesn't map onto the token scale; gating them produced false positives against legitimate layout math.

scope.escapeHatch: A raw value can still pass via an inline `stylelint-disable-next-line scale-unlimited/declaration-strict-value` comment, but the comment must state why — reviewers should treat an unexplained disable as a rejection, not a pass.

primitiveColorCheck.description: Stylelint accepts any var(), so it can't tell a primitive from a semantic token. This test closes that gap for color: component CSS that references a primitive color token - or a deprecated alias resolving to one - fails with the file, line, and token.
primitiveColorCheck.notCovered: Other primitive types are not checked. No component CSS references a primitive dimension token today, but nothing enforces that yet. Component tokens may alias dimension primitives (see the component token JSON files); that is the token layer, not component CSS.

sourceFormat.format: DTCG 2025.10 standard token data; separate CSS recipes
sourceFormat.casingPolicy: Preserve authored casing. Uppercase or other casing controls require a new design decision.
